title: Luke: good news for the lost
note: Rebuilt on 2026-11-26 from the Bible Explorer film of the same slug. New wording, same facts: each claim is in the old film's captions or its 'differ' note, whose sources are in docs/work/elite/explorer-ledger.md. Scripture is the Berean Standard Bible, checked against client/public/bible/text/ by film/tools/write-script.py.

lines: Luke opens with a formal preface. Many have written accounts. The material was handed down by eyewitnesses. And he has investigated everything carefully.
It's the first of two books by the same author, and it presents Jesus as Savior.
Today in the city of David a Savior has been born to you.

scripture.text: Today in the city of David a Savior has been born to you.

lines: After the births of John and Jesus comes the ministry in Galilee. Then the turning point is marked in the text, and the long central section is framed as the road to Jerusalem.
The book ends where it began, in the temple.

scripture.text: Jesus resolutely set out for Jerusalem.

chapters.kicker: Watch for: people others passed over
lines: Luke gives more attention to wealth and poverty than any other Gospel, and women are prominent throughout. Samaritans, tax collectors, and sinners are welcomed.
In his first sermon, Jesus reads from Isaiah and says it's fulfilled that day.

scripture.text: He has anointed Me to preach good news to the poor.

lines: The parables of the lost sheep, the lost coin, and the lost son show God's joy in finding the lost. They also expose the resentment of those who think they were never lost.
Jesus sums up the whole book in one line.
For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost.

scripture.text: For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost.

lines: Luke shows Jesus praying at the turning points of his life: at his baptism, before choosing the Twelve, at the transfiguration, in Gethsemane, and on the cross.
Prayer in Luke is the ordinary posture of those who wait on God.
The word today carries weight in Luke. Salvation is present, not only future, and it brings joy.
On the Emmaus road, the risen Jesus opens the Scriptures to two disciples who had been hoping, and had given up.

scripture.text: Were not our hearts burning within us as He spoke with us on the road

lines: Start with chapter one. The key chapters are one, two, four, fifteen, nineteen, and twenty-four. Watch the meals, the prayers, and the word today.
And read on. The same author's second book is Acts.
